items.title: El Sabadell solo recupera a Catalá para la visita a Leganés
items.description: El Sabadell viajará a Butarque con pocas novedades en cuanto a disponibilidad de efectivos. Respecto al último partido, contra el Granada, solo recuperan a José Luis Catalá, que vuelve a estar disponible después de cumplir un partido de sanción por la tarjeta roja que vio ante el Eldense. Fue expulsado apenas un minuto después de sustituir a Bonaldo, que abandonó el campo lesionado. Precisamente, la baja del central brasileño es una de las novedades negativas de la semana. Las pruebas médicas han confirmado que estará unas semanas apartado de los terrenos de juego después de que se resintiera de unas molestias que ya había notado durante un entrenamiento. "Pensábamos que se quedaría en eso, pero finalmente en Elda se resintió", ha explicado el técnico arlequinado. Tampoco estará disponible Quadri; aunque su evolución está siendo favorable, no quieren precipitar su regreso, ya que "lo más importante es su salud". El objetivo es que pueda reincorporarse pronto, aunque todavía no hay una fecha confirmada. "Confío en que la semana que viene veremos si puede estar para el partido de Copa o para el de Liga". Otra de las ausencias será Urri, que arrastra desde hace unas semanas unos problemas articulares en la rodilla que le están impidiendo competir con normalidad. Se trata de unas molestias que ya tenía la pasada temporada, aunque estaban controladas, y han ido aumentando progresivamente. Su regreso es una incógnita, ya que no se puede establecer un periodo de recuperación concreto. "No es un tema muscular, sino articular. Tenemos que ir viendo cómo evoluciona", ha explicado el entrenador. A estas tres bajas se suman las de Nuamah, con sus problemas de isquiotibiales, y Xavi Moreno, que sigue recuperándose del esguince de tobillo que le ha impedido jugar en los últimos nueve partidos de liga. La nota positiva es que los futbolistas que ya forzaron para estar ante el Granada han seguido acumulando entrenamientos y ganando ritmo competitivo. Eneko Aguilar y Miki Codina tuvieron minutos ante el Granada, mientras que Pipa estuvo en el banquillo. "Fue precipitado, pero la situación era la que era y necesitábamos efectivos. Han completado bien la semana y van ganando ritmo", ha destacado el técnico.

Formé au Real Madrid, il a franchi un cap en rejoignant Dortmund en prêt, avant son transfert à l'Inter Milan. items.description: European Leagues ha celebrado su 53ª Asamblea General, donde se ha marcado un hito en la gobernanza de la organización. Las ligas que forman parte de la misma han aprobado por unanimidad el nombramiento de Beatriz Álvarez, presidenta de Liga F, como primera representante de la Plataforma de Ligas Femeninas Miembro en el Consejo de Administración de European Leagues. El nombramiento supone un paso importante para reforzar la representación del fútbol femenino de ámbito nacional en los órganos de decisión de la organización y garantiza que las ligas femeninas cuenten con voz propia para trasladar sus perspectivas e intereses al más alto nivel de la organización.

items.title: Gerard López y su espina clavada en el Barça: "No rendí como en Valencia"
items.description: Gerard López (Granollers, 12 de marzo de 1979) atraviesa un momento de gran actividad mediática. Colaborador de Movistar Plus, donde analiza y comenta los partidos de la Champions League, transmite en cada intervención su pasión por el fútbol y su facilidad para explicar y desgranar el juego. Estos días, entre viajes y compromisos profesionales, pasó por la redacción de Mundo Deportivo para participar en el espacio de entrevistas 'Café Culé'. Llegó con las prisas propias de una agenda apretada, pero sin perder la sonrisa ni dejar de saludar a quienes se cruzaban en su camino. El fútbol lo lleva dentro, y no es casualidad: en su familia, residente en Granollers, siempre se vivió con pasión. Tres hermanos, Sergi, Juli y Gerard el menor de ellos, tres futbolistas que pasaron por la mejor escuela del mundo: la Masia del Barça.

Olympiacos go into this match unbeaten in their last three outings. They drew 0-0 with Rennes on November 4, having beaten Sparta 1-0 on October 22 and Marseille 1-0 on October 15. That run of clean sheets and narrow wins gives them a platform to push for a result that would strengthen their European standing.
AC Milan arrive in much rockier form. They lost 0-2 to Ferencvaros on November 5 and fell 0-3 to Bournemouth on October 22, though they did show their quality with a 4-0 win over Red Bull on October 15. Back-to-back defeats make this trip to Greece a chance to stop the slide and salvage momentum in the competition.
Olympiacos projected lineup
Olympiacos line up in a 4-2-3-1 with Stefan Ortega behind a back four of Manolis Saliakas, Panagiotis Retsos, David Carmo and Onyemaechi Bruno. Remo Freuler and Gustavo Sa sit as the double pivot, screening for an attacking trio of Paschalis Toufakis, Gelson Martins and Konstantinos Fortounis behind lone striker Armando Gonzalez. With no absences listed, this looks like a full-strength selection built on the defensive solidity that produced three straight clean sheets, or near enough, in their last run of results, and the width from Martins and Fortounis should look to stretch Milan’s back line.
Olympiacos projected starting XI (4-2-3-1): Stefan Ortega, Manolis Saliakas, Panagiotis Retsos, David Carmo, Onyemaechi Bruno, Remo Freuler, Gustavo Sa, Paschalis Toufakis, Gelson Martins, Armando Gonzalez, Konstantinos Fortounis.
AC Milan projected lineup
AC Milan are set up in a 4-4-1-1, with Mike Maignan in goal behind Mario Gila, Koni De Winter, Sankhoun Diawara and Pervis Estupinan. Omari Hutchinson, Ardon Jashari, Adrien Rabiot and Yunus Musah make up the midfield four, with Alphadjo Cisse just behind Goncalo Ramos up top. The team is without Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Samuel Chukwueze, Pietro Terracciano, Matteo Gabbia, Alexis Saelemaekers and Nirash Perera, a sizable list that thins out their options in midfield and at the back. Rabiot and Jashari will need to control the tempo if Milan are to avoid a third defeat in four and steady themselves in the competition.
AC Milan projected starting XI (4-4-1-1): Mike Maignan, Mario Gila, Koni De Winter, Sankhoun Diawara, Pervis Estupinan, Omari Hutchinson, Ardon Jashari, Adrien Rabiot, Yunus Musah, Alphadjo Cisse, Goncalo Ramos.

items.description: Didier Deschamps, né le 15 octobre 1968 à Bayonne, est un des rares footballeur à avoir gagné la Coupe du monde comme joueur et comme sélectionneur. Originaire du Pays basque puis formé au FC Nantes, il évolue rapidement au poste de milieu défensif sous les couleurs nantaises mais il fait l'essentiel de sa carrière à Marseille puis Turin. Après 103 sélections en bleu, une Coupe du monde et un Euro, il devient entraîneur à l'AS Monaco où il atteint la finale de la Ligue des champions. Il remporte le titre de champion de Ligue 1 avec l'OM. Depuis 2012, il est le sélectionneur de l'équipe de France qu'il a mené au titre mondial en 2018. Il a quitté ses fonctions à l'issue de la Coupe du monde 2026, cédant sa place à Zinedine Zidane.

items.title: Galaxia II
items.description: Un día escribí que Giuliano Simeone, más pundonor que talento, espabilaba a sus compañeros y les contagiaba su ímpetu, su garra, su agónica lucha por llegar a balones imposibles. Les ponía banderillas negras por encoger la pierna. Salvando las distancias, porque la calidad es un grado, el superlativo Jude Bellingham cambió el signo del partido contra el PSV, secundado por Arda Güler, la perla turca. Jude es un genio que corre como un demonio; domina el frente de ataque, ordena y manda en los medios, firma sus pases con preaviso de gol y en ocasiones como la presente rubrica con un tanto que es una obra de arte. Entró desde el banquillo tras el descanso y la luz se hizo.

items.title: Un campo talismán para el Athletic
items.description: El Athletic visita este sábado un campo talismán. Después de la dura derrota encajada en San Mamés ante el Espanyol, los rojiblancos tienen la oportunidad de resarcirse en la Rosaleda, el estadio donde derrotaron al Real Madrid en la semifinal de la Supercopa ganada en 2021, con Marcelino García Toral al frente de banquillo pocos días después de la destitución de Gaizka Garitano. La salida del deriotarra se produjo el 3 de enero y el partido contra los blancos en plena pandemia se disputó el día 14. Los leones jugaron una buena primera mitad para acabar ganando 1-2 gracias al doblete anotado por Raúl García antes del descanso. Benzema recortó distancias en el minuto 73’ pero los leones supieron sufrir para lograr un puesto en la final.

items.description: El Barça cumplió, en la fría tarde de Azerbaiyán, todos sus objetivos básicos. Ganó los tres puntos (1-4), sumó tres goles más en el ‘gol average’ tan determinante en el formato actual de la Champions y Flick pudo rotar la plantilla. Lamine Yamal se quedó en casa, Raphinha en el banquillo y el Barça salió con cinco jugadores poco o nada habituales en la alineación titular: Koundé, Balde, Gavi, Gabriel Jesus y Adeyemi. Y con esta alineación, propia de octavos de final de Copa, la noche salió redonda. También es cierto que el Sabah, por sorpresa de todos, también rotó contra el Barça. El entrenador lituano reservó a sus dos mejores jugadores: Mickels y Simic, que habían sumado diez goles en la fase de clasificación de la Champions, chuparon banquillo.

items.title: Gerard, Fermín y Florentino
items.description: Seguramente nunca será el jugador más destacado del partido. Es probable que su puntuación no llegue nunca al sobresaliente, pero no creo tampoco que sume un suspenso. Las actuaciones de Gerard Martin son siempre correctas, de notable alto. Y es verdad que ante el Villarreal rozó el sobresaliente por su partido impecable y además por marcar el primer gol, el gol que abrió el camino de la victoria. Gerard es de los pocos jugadores jóvenes del primer equipo que no se ha formado en la Masia. Proviene de la magnífica escuela de fútbol del Cornellà. Hansi Flck ha sido fundamental en su trayectoria. El mister siempre ha confiado en este jugador que llegó al primer equipo como lateral izquierdo y que Flick lo ha convertido en uno de los mejores centrales de la Liga.

items.title: Las pérdidas y los tiros libres asfixian al Barça en Europa
items.description: Ni los más viejos del lugar se acuerdan de que el Barça perdiese tres partidos europeos consecutivos en el Palau. No lo recuerdan porque no había pasado nunca. Incluso había temporadas que no perdía tres encuentros de Euroliga en casa en toda la campaña. Pero, en lo que va de curso, el equipo de Sekulic ya ha salido derrotado en 5 de 8 ocasiones en el Palau, en Euroliga. Y sí, es un equipo en formación, que apuesta por una idea clara, que puede ser divertida con tanta velocidad y tanta energía en la pista. Y sí, este es un equipo que, como ha pasado en los últimos años, acumula un sinfín de lesiones de jugadores fundamentales. Pero las derrotas consecutivas ante París (86-89), Estrella Roja (100-103) y Fenerbahçe (77-83) tienen dos denominadores comunes. Un patrón que se repite derrota tras derrota y que no es de recibo.

items.title: Pep Guardiola urges Portugal to give Cristiano Ronaldo a dignified farewell: ‘He deserves a different ending’
items.description:
Pep Guardiola says Portugal must give Cristiano Ronaldo the farewell he deserves, calling for a celebration where he feels the love of his country and leave through the front door. 
Pep Guardiola has joined the conversation about Cristiano Ronaldo‘s departure from the Portugal national team, and the Spanish coach did not hold back in calling for a proper goodbye for the forward.



In an interview with Brazilian legend Romario, Guardiola said that the situation has to end well and that Portugal cannot let Ronaldo leave the national team in this manner.



“Cristiano cannot leave in this way, the Portuguese national team cannot let him leave like this,” Guardiola said. According to the coach, Ronaldo has been an important figure, not only for himself and for Portugal, but for the future generations of Portuguese players, who should see that a player of his stature leaves the way he deserves.



“There are very special players and Cristiano has been one of them,” he added, saying that the federation has to fix the situation and that, although it is not his problem, it has to be fixed.



#مترجم | بيب غوارديولا يوجه رسالة إلى منتخب البرتغال بشأن الطريقة التي يجب أن يودّع بها كريستيانو رونالدو! ❤️"لا يمكن للمنتخب البرتغالي أن يودّع كريستيانو بهذه الطريقة، إنه يستحق وداعًا يليق به." pic.twitter.com/squrRlOeQO— الدوري الإنجليزي™ (@TrendEPL) November 25, 2026 



Guardiola’s words come after a turbulent end to Ronaldo’s international career. The forward walked out of the national team’s camp in September after a dispute with coach Jorge Jesus and announced his retirement on November 5, finishing with 146 goals in 234 matches. 



Portugal paid tribute to him before the match against Denmark in Braga on November 14, but without Ronaldo present, and the federation has promised a farewell event for which no date has been announced.


        


Guardiola’s vision of the farewell Ronaldo deserves



For Guardiola, the solution goes beyond avoiding a bad ending, as he also has a clear idea of what the goodbye should look like. The coach called for a celebration in which Ronaldo can feel the affection of his people, and he stressed that the forward must also play his part by making an effort to forget what happened in the past.



“A career is not judged by a month or two, or by an understanding or lack of understanding with one or two people,” he said. According to Guardiola, great players “have to leave through the front door,” because they have earned it with everything they have given to the sport.



The Spanish coach also said that Ronaldo’s farewell has to serve as an example for the children who follow their idols’ careers. “‘I want to leave one day like Romario did, like Cristiano, like Messi, like Maldini, or like the great players there have been.’ That is how it has to be,” Guardiola concluded.



Guardiola’s message is a call for both sides to turn the page, so that Ronaldo’s 23 years with Portugal are remembered for what they achieved and not for how they ended. With the federation having promised a tribute, the challenge now is to turn that pledge into a farewell worthy of the country’s all-time leading scorer.

items.title: Sporting vs Manchester United: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League match
items.description:
Take a look at the confirmed lineups for Sporting vs Manchester United in the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League. Sporting host Manchester United at a venue where both sides are searching for the kind of form that settles a Champions League group night rather than complicates it.
Sporting arrive on the back of a 1-0 win over Shakhtar Donetsk on November 3, which followed a 2-3 loss to LASK on October 21 and a 2-0 win over Lens on October 13. The Shakhtar result snapped the stumble against LASK and gave them a platform heading into this fixture. A positive result here would put Sporting in a strong position in the group with momentum behind them.
Manchester United come into this one off a 3-2 win over Roma on November 3, sandwiched between a 1-4 loss to Como 1907 on October 21 and a 0-2 loss to Atlético on October 13. The win over Roma arrested a run of two straight defeats and offered some reassurance after a difficult stretch. Another win on the road would go a long way toward steadying their campaign.
Sporting confirmed lineup
Sporting line up in a 4-3-3 with Kaique in goal behind a back four of Iván Fresneda, Eduardo Quaresma, Gonçalo Inácio and Maxi Araújo. Sergi Altimira, Silas Andersen and Issa Doumbia make up the midfield, giving them both defensive cover and progression through the center. Up front, Luís Suárez leads the line with Geny Catamo and Luís Guilherme providing width and pace in behind him. Nuno Santos and Zeno Debast are both out, which thins their options on the left side and in defense.
Sporting confirmed starting XI (4-3-3): Kaique, Iván Fresneda, Maxi Araújo, Sergi Altimira, Eduardo Quaresma, Gonçalo Inácio, Silas Andersen, Issa Doumbia, Luís Suárez, Geny Catamo, Luís Guilherme.
Manchester United confirmed lineup
Manchester United set up in a 3-4-2-1, with Senne Lammens behind a back three of Lisandro Martínez, Harry Maguire and Leny Yoro. Noussair Mazraoui and Amad Diallo provide the width as wing-backs, with Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans holding the center of midfield. Bruno Fernandes and Bryan Mbeumo sit just behind Joshua Zirkzee, who leads the line as the central striker. The absences of Marcus Rashford, Carlos Baleba, Benjamin Šeško, Manuel Ugarte and Matheus Cunha leave them without several attacking and midfield options, putting more responsibility on the players selected tonight.
Manchester United confirmed starting XI (3-4-2-1): Senne Lammens, Amad Diallo, Noussair Mazraoui, Lisandro Martínez, Harry Maguire, Leny Yoro, Kobbie Mainoo, Youri Tielemans, Joshua Zirkzee, Bryan Mbeumo, Bruno Fernandes.

items.title: Atletico Madrid vs Viking: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Atletico Madrid vs Viking in the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League. Atletico Madrid host Viking in the Champions League with both sides looking to settle their place in this season’s league phase, and the contrast in European pedigree adds an extra layer to a game that should otherwise favor the hosts on paper.
Atletico Madrid come into this one off a 0-2 loss to Bayern on November 3, following a 1-1 draw with Stuttgart on October 20 and a 2-0 win over Man U on October 13. The alternating results point to a team still finding consistency in a tough European group. A home win would steady things and keep their qualification hopes firmly in their own hands.
Viking arrive on the back of a 4-1 win over Sabah FK on November 4, sandwiched between a 1-3 defeat to Aston Villa on October 21 and a 3-3 draw with Bayern on October 13. That draw with Bayern showed they can compete with elite opposition, even if the Aston Villa result exposed some fragility. A positive result in Madrid would be the clearest sign yet that Viking belong at this level.
Atletico Madrid confirmed lineup
Diego Simeone sets his team up in a 4-4-2, with Jan Oblak behind a back line of Marcos Llorente, Robin Le Normand, Dávid Hancko and Alex Grimaldo. Johnny Cardoso and Pablo Barrios anchor the midfield alongside Giuliano Simeone and Álex Baena, feeding Julián Alvarez and Lee Kang-in up top. The absences of Cristian Romero, Alejandro Grimaldo and Ademola Lookman thin out their depth at the back and in attack, putting more responsibility on the players stepping into the lineup to maintain the team’s usual balance.
Atletico Madrid confirmed starting XI (4-4-2): Jan Oblak, Marcos Llorente, Alejandro Grimaldo, Koke, Robin Le Normand, Dávid Hancko, Lee Kang-In, Johnny Cardoso, Alexander Sørloth, Julián Alvarez, Álex Baena.
Viking confirmed lineup
Bjarte Lunde Aarsheim goes with a 4-3-3 for Viking, built around Arild Ostbo in goal and a back four of Henrik Heggheim, Gianni Stensness, Henrik Falchener and Vetle Auklend. Joe Bell, Tobias Moi and Kristoffer Askildsen make up the midfield trio, with Peter Christiansen, Erik Botheim and Zlatko Tripić leading the front line. With no absences to account for, Aarsheim can select his strongest available group and ask his front three to stretch an Atletico Madrid defense missing some of its regular personnel.
Viking confirmed starting XI (4-3-3): Ľubomír Belko, Herman Haugen, Henrik Heggheim, Tobias Moi, Gianni Stensness, Henrik Falchener, Kristoffer Askildsen, Simen Kvia-Egeskog, Erik Botheim, Henrik Bjørdal, Zlatko Tripić.

items.title: Club Brugge vs Liverpool: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Club Brugge vs Liverpool in the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League. Club Brugge host Liverpool at a venue where goals have been easy to come by for both sides this season, and this Champions League clash looks unlikely to be short of chances.
Club Brugge arrive on a strong run of form. They beat PSV 2-1 on November 4, following up a 3-0 win over Lens on October 21 and a wild 4-3 win over Inter on October 13. Three straight victories, including two shootout-style scorelines, have given Ivan Leko’s side real momentum heading into this European test.
Liverpool come into this one off a setback. They lost 2-3 to Fenerbahce on November 4, after a 4-3 win over Villarreal on October 20 and a 6-3 win over LASK on October 14. The defeat snapped a run of high-scoring wins, and Liverpool will want to get back on track against a Brugge side that has been in good touch.
Club Brugge confirmed lineup
Ivan Leko sets Club Brugge up in a 4-1-4-1, with Yann Sommer behind a back four of Kyriani Sabbe, Jorne Spileers, Brandon Mechele and Joaquin Seys. Freddie Potts sits as the lone holding midfielder, screening for a busy four ahead of him in Carlos Forbs, Hugo Vetlesen, Hans Vanaken and Félix Lemaréchal, with Vanaken’s experience central to how they link play into Nicolò Tresoldi up top. There are no absences to work around, so Leko can pick his strongest available group, and the shape allows Brugge to push numbers forward quickly given their recent scoring form.
Club Brugge confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Yann Sommer, Kyriani Sabbe, Joaquin Seys, Hans Vanaken, Jorne Spileers, Brandon Mechele, Carlos Forbs, Freddie Potts, Nicolò Tresoldi, Hugo Vetlesen, Félix Lemaréchal.
Liverpool confirmed lineup
Andoni Iraola lines Liverpool up in a 4-2-3-1, with Alisson in goal behind Jeremie Frimpong, Jérémy Jacquet, Joe Gomez and Kostas Tsimikas. Alexis Mac Allister and Dominik Szoboszlai form the double pivot, with Treymaurice Nyoni, Víctor Muñoz and Bradley Barcola supporting Rio Ngumoha as the central striker. The team is missing Ryan Gravenberch, Conor Bradley, Giovanni Leoni, Amara Nallo and Hugo Ekitiké, a significant list that affects both midfield depth and the center-forward options, leaving Ngumoha to lead the line rather than a recognized number nine.
Liverpool confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Alisson Becker, Jeremie Frimpong, Miloš Kerkez, Dominik Szoboszlai, Jérémy Jacquet, Ronald Araujo, Víctor Muñoz, Trey Nyoni, Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola.

items.title: Why is Raphinha not starting for Barcelona vs Sabah in 2026-27 UEFA Champions League?
items.description:
Raphinha starts on the bench for Barcelona's Champions League trip to Sabah as Hansi Flick rotates his lineup and hands a first start together to Gabriel Jesus, Karim Adeyemi and Anthony Gordon. 
Raphinha begins Barcelona’s Champions League match against Sabah in Azerbaijan on the bench, a surprising decision from Hansi Flick on matchday five of the league phase, in a game that already comes with the absence of Lamine Yamal.



Everything seems to indicate that the decision responds to rotation and workload management rather than a physical problem. No new injury has been reported for Raphinha, who is available in the matchday squad and comes off a big effort in the 3-2 comeback win over Villarreal last weekend, which may have prompted Flick to give him a rest.



In his place, Flick opted for a completely new front line, with Gabriel Jesus as the central striker and Karim Adeyemi and Anthony Gordon on the wings, marking the first time the three start together for Barcelona.



Barcelona arrive in the match sitting eighth in the league phase with nine points, and they need a victory to keep climbing toward the top. Raphinha remains on the bench as an option for the second half, and with Deportivo A Coruna awaiting on Sunday, Flick’s plan appears to be to keep his key players fresh across a demanding schedule.




🚨 𝗕𝗔𝗥𝗖̧𝗔 𝗫𝗜 🚨 pic.twitter.com/hr9kRfExTr— FC Barcelona (@FCBarcelona_es) November 25, 2026




Barcelona’s confirmed lineup vs Sabah



Flick made five changes compared to the team that started the 3-2 win over Villarreal last weekend. Alejandro Balde and Jules Kounde come into the defense in place of Eric Garcia and Joao Cancelo, while Gavi takes the spot of Marc Bernal in midfield.


        


Up front, Jesus and Gordon replace Yamal and Raphinha, the former due to his ankle problem and the latter in what appears to be a rotation decision. Joan Garcia, Gerard Martin, Frenkie de Jong, Pedri, Fermin Lopez and Adeyemi keep their places, while Pau Cubarsi starts on the bench.



Barcelona’s confirmed lineup: Joan Garcia; Jules Kounde, Frenkie de Jong, Gerard Martin, Alejandro Balde; Gavi, Pedri, Fermin Lopez; Karim Adeyemi, Gabriel Jesus, Anthony Gordon.

items.title: Sabah FK vs Barcelona: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Sabah FK vs Barcelona in the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League. This Champions League pairing puts a club from Baku on home soil against one of the biggest names in the competition, with Sabah FK needing far more than effort to trouble Barcelona on this occasion.
Sabah come into this one on a rough run, having lost 1-4 to Viking on November 4 and 1-2 to Dortmund on October 20, with their 2-0 win over Slavia Praha on October 13 now a fading memory. The two straight defeats have piled on the pressure, and a home game against a side of Barcelona‘s stature is a tough place to try to turn things around. Anything taken from this match would count as a major result for Valdas Dambrauskas and his group.
Barcelona arrive in much better shape, having beaten Aston Villa 3-0 on November 3 after a 2-4 loss to PSG on October 20 and a 4-1 win over Galatasaray on October 13. The home defeat to PSG stands out as their one blemish in this stretch, but they bounced back in convincing fashion against Villa. A win in Baku would keep them firmly on track in the group phase.
Sabah FK confirmed lineup
Dambrauskas sets Sabah up in a 4-2-3-1, with Stas Pokatilov behind a back line of Akim Zedadka, Steve Solvet, Rahman Dashdamirov and Tymoteusz Puchacz. Umarali Rakhmonaliev and Du Queiroz sit as the double pivot, screening in front of the defense against a Barcelona side with plenty of attacking quality to handle. Ivan Lepinjica, Christian Nwachukwu and Orphé Mbina operate across the attacking midfield band behind lone striker Joy-Lance Mickels, a setup built to stay compact and look for chances on the counter. Aden McCarthy is out for the hosts, one absence Dambrauskas has to account for in his planning.
Sabah FK confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Stas Pokatilov, Akim Zedadka, Tymoteusz Puchacz, Ivan Lepinjica, Steve Solvet, Júnior Almeida, Xander Severina, Umarali Rakhmonaliev, Xayal Aliyev, Du Queiroz, Christian Nwachukwu. Coach: Valdas Dambrauskas.
Barcelona confirmed lineup
Hansi Flick also goes with a 4-2-3-1, with Joan García in goal behind a back four of Eric García, Pau Cubarsí, Gerard Martín and João Cancelo. Pedri and Marc Bernal pair up in midfield, giving Barcelona control in the center of the pitch, while Fermín López pushes forward to support the front line. Karim Adeyemi, Raphinha and Anthony Gordon form the attacking trio behind the central attacking midfield slot, with pace and directness on both flanks. Barcelona are notably playing without Lamine Yamal today while also missing Rodri, Xavi Espart, Roony Bardghji, Juan Hernández and Jordi Pesquer.
Barcelona confirmed starting XI (4-3-3): Joan García, Jules Koundé, Alejandro Balde, Gavi, Frenkie de Jong, Gerard Martín, Fermín López, Pedri, Gabriel Jesus, Karim Adeyemi, Anthony Gordon. Coach: Hansi Flick.

items.title: Premier League’s burst of early sendings-off may not last – but red cards are on the rise for a reason
items.description: While referees tend to reach for red early in the season before easing off, players are under increasing pressure to keep pace in a frenetic environmentOff! Off! Off! The past three Premier League games have featured a red card, each for a different reason. Brighton’s Costinha was sent off for two bookings at Hull, Leny Yoro collected a red card against Liverpool for denying a goalscoring opportunity (though his suspension was overturned on appeal) and James Tarkowski saw red for serious foul play at Brentford.This season is shaping up to be an outlier in the VAR era of officiating in English football. The latest red cards took the Premier League total to 22 in 2026-27. The rate of 0.2 per game equates to 76 across the whole season, which would equal the Premier League record set in 2005-06. Refereeing has evolved in the past decade, though. The average across the seven completed campaigns since VAR was introduced is 0.12 per game, with a high of 0.15 in 2023-24. Continue reading...

items.title: Senegal regaining Afcon title is the right end to fiasco but issues do not stop there | Osasu Obayiuwana
items.description: After African football was dragged into needless disrepute the next step is to tackle two key areas of governanceA journey of 310 days and three legal proceedings to confirm two things we know – that Senegal beat Morocco 1-0 to win the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations and, most importantly, that the decision of a referee remains final and sacrosanct – has produced the longest, most comical and embarrassing Afcon final in the tournament’s 69-year history.As the Confederation of African Football (Caf) executive committee member Samir Sobha told the Guardian, the decision of the organisation’s appeals board in March to overturn Senegal’s victory and award the title to Morocco, prompting a legal charade ended by the court of arbitration for sport’s verdict on Tuesday, was a “big joke” that brought Caf and the Afcon into needless disrepute. items.title: Will Hajime Moriyasu get a high-profile job in Europe after his eight years in charge of Japan?
items.description: The coach will leave early after the postponement of the Asian Cup and, while there has been clear progress, some had hoped for better results at World CupsA popular Christmas tradition in Japan is to head to KFC but there is an unexpected item on the menu to chew over this year for the millions who do so – a meaty debate over Hajime Moriyasu’s eight years as national-team head coach. Among the many consequences of the Asian Cup’s postponement from January 2027 to December is the fact his tenure has ended early.The 58-year-old was supposed to stay on until February to cap that lengthy spell with (hopefully) a deserved trophy, hand over to Go Oiwa and then, perhaps, blaze a trail to Europe. Instead he left this month, after 113 games in charge during which Japan became a global force to be reckoned with, even if there are those who think he underdelivered. Continue reading...

items.title: Mbappe joins Ronaldo and Messi in an elite Champions League club, but falls short of the Argentine in one record
items.description:
Kylian Mbappe joined Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi in the 75-goal Champions League club, and his scoring streak with Real Madrid put him in rare company. 
Kylian Mbappe reached a historic milestone in the Champions League by scoring twice in Real Madrid’s 5-1 win over PSV Eindhoven, a brace that took him to 75 goals in the competition. The French forward now belongs to an exclusive group of scorers, led by Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi, although there is one record he could not take from the Argentine.



Mbappe‘s goals came in the second half at the Santiago Bernabeu, in the 64th and 84th minutes, after Real Madrid had gone behind to a penalty from Ivan Perisic in the first half.



Federico Valverde equalized early in the second half, Jude Bellingham put the hosts in front, and Mbappe then extended the lead before Vinicius Junior sealed the result in the 87th minute.



Those two goals took him to 75, a mark that only four players had previously reached in the competition: Cristiano Ronaldo with 140, Messi with 129, Robert Lewandowski with 109 and Karim Benzema with 90. The difference with Messi lies in age, as the Argentine reached the mark at 27 years and 169 days, while Mbappe did it at 27 years and 339 days. 




Mbappé POTM 🏆#UCL pic.twitter.com/xPfmL8zO3x— UEFA Champions League (@ChampionsLeague) November 24, 2026




That makes the Frenchman the second-youngest player to get there, behind only Messi, although he still has time to keep adding to his total in a season in which he already has 19 goals in 18 matches for the club.



Mbappe also makes history with his scoring streak


        


Mbappe’s brace extended a run that was already historic. The French forward has now scored in five consecutive matchdays in this season’s Champions League, something that only Cristiano Ronaldo had achieved for Real Madrid, back in 2017-18.



He has also scored in seven straight games in the competition, being the first French player in history to reach this mark, and he is now second in the club’s history, behind only Ronaldo’s 11 consecutive matches.



His streak also places him in very select company across the competition. Only five players have scored in seven or more consecutive Champions League matches for their club: Ronaldo with 11 for Real Madrid in 2017-18, Harry Kane with eight for Bayern Munich in 2026, Mbappe with seven and counting for Real Madrid in 2026, and Sebastien Haller (Ajax, 2021-22) and Edinson Cavani (PSG, 2016-17) with seven each.



With his scoring streak still alive and Real Madrid sitting among the leaders of the league phase, Mbappe will look to keep adding to his Champions League total, and to keep closing the gap on the few names ahead of him.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo helps Al Nassr beat Al Sadd, but remains far from the AFC Golden Boot race
items.description:
Cristiano Ronaldo helps Al Nassr beat Al Sadd, but his two goals in the AFC Champions League Elite leave the Golden Boot race well out of reach for now. 
Cristiano Ronaldo led Al Nassr to a 2-1 win over Al Sadd in the AFC Champions League Elite, opening the scoring from the penalty spot, but the goal does little to bring him closer to the top of the competition’s scoring chart. The Portuguese forward has two goals this season in the tournament, and the race for the Golden Boot appears to be moving further out of his reach.



Ronaldo’s penalty in the 13th minute put Al Nassr in front, although Mohammed Waad equalized for Al Sadd in the 22nd minute. When the match looked set to get complicated, Joao Felix stepped up with a spectacular bicycle kick to score the winning goal, giving his team a great result for the standings.



Although Cristiano took home a goal, he remains a considerable distance from the leaders. The gap grew even wider on the same night, as the two forwards at the top of the list both scored a brace in their respective games.



Prince Ampem netted twice in Shanghai Port’s 3-1 win over Buriram United and now leads the chart with eight goals, while Julian Quinones also scored twice in Al Qadsiah’s 5-1 victory over Shabab Al Ahli, moving up to six goals.




No stopping that. ⚡Cristiano Ronaldo with an emphatic finish from the spot! #ACLElite | #NSRvSAD pic.twitter.com/h9tWOC042Y— #ACLElite | #ACLTwo (@TheAFCCL) November 24, 2026




That leaves Ronaldo six goals behind Ampem and four behind Quinones, with Brayan Perea and Houssine Rahimi also ahead of him on five. Al Nassr still have matches left in the league phase, and the captain has played one fewer game than the leaders, as the team still has to play its pending match against Al Wasl.



Ronaldo ties a historic Al Nassr mark in the AFC Champions League Elite


        


Beyond the race for the Golden Boot, Ronaldo’s penalty against Al Sadd also brings a milestone for Al Nassr’s history book. The strike took him to 16 goals in the AFC Champions League Elite, matching the club’s record held by Moroccan forward Abderrazak Hamdallah, who had been the team’s top scorer in the competition.



However, the tie is only part of the story. Ronaldo also scored in the AFC Champions League Two, against Al Wasl in the quarterfinals in 2026, and that goal takes him to 17 in continental competitions, one more than Hamdallah. That makes the Portuguese forward Al Nassr’s outright top scorer in continental tournaments, even if he is only level in the Elite.



Even if the Golden Boot looks out of reach for now, Ronaldo has plenty to play for with Al Nassr, who are still climbing in the league phase and have matches left to improve their position. With a continental record already in his pocket and 13 goals to go before reaching 1,000, the captain keeps adding milestones to a season in which every goal carries extra weight.

items.description:
The French winger's latest appearance ended far sooner than expected, raising fresh concerns about his fitness as the Saudi side continues its pursuit of domestic and continental success. 
Cristiano Ronaldo and Al-Nassr secured another important AFC Champions League Elite victory against Al-Sadd, but the celebrations at Al-Awwal Park were overshadowed by an early setback involving Kingsley Coman. The French winger’s latest appearance ended far sooner than expected, raising fresh concerns about his fitness as the Saudi side continues its pursuit of domestic and continental success.



Al-Nassr eventually claimed a 2-1 victory on Tuesday, thanks to Ronaldo’s penalty and a spectacular overhead kick from Joao Felix. However, Coman’s departure after only a few minutes left Ange Postecoglou with another potential injury problem to manage. Ronaldo opened the scoring from the penalty spot in the 13th minute after being fouled inside the area by Mohamed Camara. 



The Portuguese forward calmly converted to register his 987th career goal, moving within 13 strikes of the historic 1,000-goal milestone. Al-Sadd responded through Mohammed Waad, who finished Akram Afif’s clever attacking move in the 22nd minute. However, the goalscorer went from hero to villain shortly before half-time, receiving a straight red card after a VAR review found that he had spat at Al-Nassr defender Nawaf Boushal. 



Despite playing against 10 men, Ange Postecoglou’s players struggled to completely dominate the visitors. Joao Felix eventually provided the decisive moment in the 52nd minute, producing a stunning bicycle kick from the edge of the penalty area that left goalkeeper Meshaal Barsham with no chance.



PLUS QUE 13 BUTS AVANT LES 1000 🔥🐐Cristiano Ronaldo 🇵🇹 a inscrit son 987e en carrière et permet à Al Nassr de prendre les devants face à Al Sadd 🇶🇦 en AFC Ligue des Champions Élite ! pic.twitter.com/JIQ9XKvmuY— SPL 🇸🇦 (@ActuSPL) November 24, 2026 



The victory moved Al-Nassr to nine points and fifth place in the AFC Champions League Elite West Region standings, with a postponed fixture against Al-Wasl still to come. Al-Sadd remained 14th with only two points from five matches.



Coman suffers another frustrating setback



The biggest concern for Postecoglou came almost immediately after kick-off, when Coman went down following an early sprint and challenge. The French winger was unable to continue and was replaced by Abdullah Al-Hamdan after just three minutes.



The timing was particularly frustrating because the Frenchman was making his first start since returning from a previous injury. The 30-year-old had only recently rejoined the squad, coming off the bench against Al-Ahli before being handed an opportunity from the beginning against Al-Sadd.



Coman substituído com apenas 5 minutos de jogo. pic.twitter.com/BwxGNH41TT— Central do Arabão (@centraldoarabao) November 24, 2026 



His latest setback raises further questions about his physical condition and ability to maintain consistency. Coman has made only nine appearances for Al-Nassr this season, scoring once without registering an assist.



Recovery timeline emerges amid hamstring injury concerns



According to an update shared by Saudi physiotherapist Thamer Al-Shahrani, Coman may have suffered a hamstring injury during a sprint. The assessment remains preliminary, with the exact severity still needing to be established through medical examinations. Al-Shahrani explained on X (formerly Twitter): “Coman has a hamstring injury from the sprint. If it’s a muscle tear, the likely recovery times are: Best case: 10-14 days. Worst case: 4-6 weeks.”



That would leave Al-Nassr facing two very different possibilities depending on the results of further assessments. A minor injury could sideline Coman for around two weeks, while a more serious muscle tear could keep him out for up to six weeks.



Kingsley Coman of team Al Nassr is tackled by Paulo Otavio of team Al Sadd SC 



The winger’s previous injury makes the situation particularly concerning. He suffered a hamstring problem during Al-Nassr’s 3-1 Champions League Elite victory over Neftchi Fergana in October, which forced him to miss several Saudi Pro League fixtures and another continental match.



Coman’s recurring fitness problems are becoming an unwanted complication for Postecoglou, who needs his attacking options available as Al-Nassr competes on multiple fronts. The Frenchman arrived with considerable expectations, but his limited availability has made it difficult for him to establish consistent momentum alongside Ronaldo, Felix and Sadio Mane.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s retirement plans after Al-Nassr contract expires take fresh twist as mother Dolores Aveiro breaks silence
items.description:
With the Portuguese superstar approaching another important crossroads at 41, fresh comments from his family have added an unexpected twist to the uncertainty surrounding the final years of his playing career. 
Cristiano Ronaldo’s future beyond his current Al-Nassr contract has become a major talking point following his retirement from international soccer. With the Portuguese superstar approaching another important crossroads at 41, fresh comments from his family have added an unexpected twist to the uncertainty surrounding the final years of his playing career.



Ronaldo remains focused on club soccer and continues to chase the remarkable milestone of 1,000 career goals. However, speculation has grown over whether the ongoing campaign will be his last in Saudi Arabia, particularly with his current agreement approaching its expiration date.



The five-time Ballon d’Or winner signed a two-year contract extension in June 2025, keeping him at Al-Nassr until the end of the 2026-27 season in June 2027. Although reports have suggested that the Saudi club would like to keep its captain for another campaign, no new agreement has been confirmed.



Ronaldo has continued producing impressive numbers, reaching 987 career goals this Tuesday. He has also scored nine times in 11 appearances across the Saudi Pro League and AFC Champions League Elite this season, maintaining his pursuit of the historic 1,000-goal mark.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Al Nassr.



His international retirement on November 5, 2026, has added another dimension to the situation. After 23 years with Portugal, he ended his international career with 234 appearances and 146 goals, allowing him to concentrate entirely on his commitments at club level.



Reports raise questions over the end of his playing career



Speculation intensified after reports suggested Ronaldo could leave Al-Nassr when his contract expires. Portuguese journalist Pedro Sepulveda previously indicated that the current campaign might represent the end of the forward’s time in Saudi Arabia. “I firmly believe that this season could be Cristiano Ronaldo’s last at Al-Nassr,” Sepulveda said, via talkSPORT.



There have also been suggestions that Al-Nassr could organize a major farewell if Ronaldo decides to leave. A possible final appearance against Al-Hilal on May 28, 2027, has been discussed, although neither his departure nor a retirement ceremony has been confirmed.



Ange Postecoglou team Manager of Al Nassr and Cristiano Ronaldo



What did Dolores Aveiro say about retirement speculation?



Ronaldo’s mother, Dolores Aveiro, has now challenged the suggestion that her son intends to retire immediately after his Al-Nassr contract expires. In comments reported by 365Scores Arabic, she directly dismissed the possibility. “It’s not true that Cristiano Ronaldo is thinking of retiring from football after his current contract with Al-Nassr expires,” Aveiro stated.



Her intervention provides a different perspective on the veteran’s plans, particularly as speculation continues over whether he will extend his stay in Riyadh. While her comments do not confirm that Ronaldo will sign another contract, they suggest that ending his playing career in June 2027 should not be treated as a foregone conclusion.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Real Madrid looks on with his mother Maria Dolores dos Santos Aveiro



Ronaldo’s decision could have consequences for Al-Nassr beyond his own career, particularly regarding the future of compatriot Joao Felix. The former Chelsea forward’s contract also runs until June 2027, and journalist Pedro Sepulveda believes his chances of remaining in Saudi Arabia could be closely connected to Ronaldo’s situation.



For now, Ronaldo has time to decide whether he wants to extend his Al-Nassr career, consider another challenge, or eventually retire. The possibility of playing alongside his son, Cristiano Jr., at senior level has also been mentioned as a potential factor in his thinking.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo sets new Al Nassr milestone with record-breaking goal vs Al Sadd
items.description:
Cristiano Ronaldo broke Abderrazak Hamdallah's record as Al Nassr's top scorer in continental competitions and moved closer to the historic mark of 1,000 career goals. 
Cristiano Ronaldo has added another record to his career by becoming Al Nassr’s all-time top scorer in continental competitions. The Portuguese forward reached the mark with his penalty against Al Sadd in the AFC Champions League Elite, a goal that also gave him his 987th in his professional career.



With the strike from the spot in the 13th minute at Al Awwal Park, Ronaldo reached 16 goals in the AFC Champions League Elite, putting him level with Abderrazak Hamdallah, the former Al Nassr forward who had held the club record. The tally by itself would have only tied the Moroccan, so the figure alone did not settle the question.



What puts Ronaldo clear at the top is a goal he scored in the AFC Champions League Two, the secondary Asian competition. It came in the quarterfinals on April 19, 2026, when he opened the scoring for Al Nassr in a 4-0 win over Al Wasl in Dubai, the 969th goal of his career at that point.



Adding it to his Elite total brings him to 17 in continental competitions, one more than Hamdallah, which makes him the club’s outright leading scorer in that category.



Cristiano Ronaldo 9️⃣8️⃣7️⃣🇵🇹🎥 @Rtiban1 pic.twitter.com/aYo1Ewvouv— Fabrizio Romano (@FabrizioRomano) November 24, 2026 



The record arrived on a night in which the captain had a point to prove, after missing a penalty in the loss to Al Ahli last Friday, a match in which he had also scored. His conversion against Al Sadd ended his run of missed penalties and gave him another landmark in a season in which he continues to chase more titles with Al Nassr in Saudi Arabia.



Where does Ronaldo stand in the race to 1,000 goals?


        


With the penalty against Al Sadd, Ronaldo moved to 987 career goals, leaving him 13 away from the historic mark of 1,000, a milestone that no player has officially reached in competitive matches.



The 41-year-old has kept up a steady pace this season, with 11 goals in 14 matches across all competitions, including a hat trick against Al Kholood on October 29 and his goal against Al Ahli last Friday.



The chase now depends almost entirely on his club form, as both he and Lionel Messi have stepped away from international duty with their national teams. Messi, for his part, is at 937 career goals, which leaves Ronaldo comfortably ahead in the race for a historic mark in soccer.

items.title: Real Madrid vs PSV: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Real Madrid vs PSV in the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League. Real Madrid host PSV at a point in the season where both sides are trying to settle into a rhythm in the Champions League, and this one pits a Madrid side on a run of wins against a PSV team still looking for consistency on the road.
Real Madrid come into this one on a three-game winning streak, having beaten AEK Athens 3-2 on November 4, Leipzig 4-1 on October 21 and Roma 4-3 on October 14. Those results have come with goals at both ends, but the outcomes have kept the points at home each time. A win here would make it four straight and tighten their grip on the top of the group picture.
PSV arrive off a mixed stretch, losing 1-2 to Brugge on November 4 after beating Porto 1-0 on October 20, and that followed a 0-1 loss to Leipzig on October 13. The Dutch side have shown they can get results against sides in and around their level, but the defeats to Brugge and Leipzig point to problems against tougher opposition. Three points in Madrid would be a major statement for Peter Bosz’s team and a real boost to their path through the group.
Real Madrid confirmed lineup
Mourinho sets Real Madrid up in a 4-2-3-1 with Courtois behind a back four of Valverde, Militão, Rüdiger and Cucurella. Tchouaméni and Camavinga sit as the double pivot, giving the side control in midfield, while Brahim Díaz and Yan Diomande support Mbappé and Vinícius Júnior further forward. With no absences listed, Mourinho has his first-choice attacking options available, and the front four carries real pace and directness in behind a PSV back line that will have to defend a lot of space.
Real Madrid confirmed starting XI (4-3-3): Thibaut Courtois, Federico Valverde, Marc Cucurella, Aurélien Tchouaméni, Éder Militão, Antonio Rüdiger, Bernardo Silva, Arda Güler, Kylian Mbappé, Yan Diomande, Vinícius Júnior. Coach: Jose Mourinho.
PSV confirmed lineup
Bosz lines PSV up in a matching 4-2-3-1, with Kovář in goal behind Dest, Geertruida, Obispo and Kostić. Sano and Mijnans anchor the midfield, with Fernández, Perišić and Til playing behind lone striker Ruben van Bommel. There are no absences to work around, so Bosz can pick his preferred XI, but the away side will need their midfield pair to hold firm against Madrid’s movement through the middle if they are to keep the game close.
PSV confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Matěj Kovář, Sergiño Dest, Filip Kostić, Kodai Sano, Lutsharel Geertruida, Armando Obispo, Ivan Perišić, Paul Wanner, Guus Til, Sven Mijnans, Ruben van Bommel. Coach: Peter Bosz.

items.title: Arsenal vs Dortmund: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League match

Take a look at the projected lineups for Arsenal vs Dortmund in the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League. Arsenal host Dortmund at the Emirates in a Champions League meeting between two sides who have found different ways to stay competitive this season.
Arsenal come into this on the back of a 2-1 win over Slavia Praha on November 4, a 2-2 draw with Bayern on October 21 and a 3-0 win over Lille on October 13. That run shows a team capable of grinding out results against tough opponents while still scoring freely when the matchup favors them. A strong showing here would keep Arsenal firmly in the mix at the top of the league phase table.
Dortmund arrive having beaten Betis 2-1 on November 4, a follow-up to a 2-1 win over Sabah FK on October 20, though they did lose 0-1 to Bodo Glimt back on October 14. The two wins either side of that defeat suggest Dortmund have settled into a rhythm after a rocky patch. Three points in London would be a significant statement for a side looking to prove they belong among the competition’s top sides.
Arsenal confirmed lineup
Arteta sets Arsenal up in a 4-2-3-1 with Kepa in goal behind a back line of Ben White, Ezri Konsa, Gabriel Magalhães and Piero Hincapié. Declan Rice and Martín Odegaard anchor the midfield, with Odegaard pushed into a more advanced creative role alongside Myles Lewis-Skelly and Noni Madueke supporting Viktor Gyökeres up top. Christos Tzolis rounds out the attacking line, giving Arsenal width and pace to work off Gyökeres as the central reference point.
Arsenal confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Kepa Arrizabalaga, Ben White, Piero Hincapié, Declan Rice, Ezri Konsa, Gabriel Magalhães, Noni Madueke, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Viktor Gyökeres, Martin Ødegaard, Christos Tzolis. Coach: Mikel Arteta.
Dortmund confirmed lineup
Kovač goes with a 3-4-2-1 shape for Dortmund, with Gregor Kobel behind a back three of Kouakou Joane Gadou, Nico Schlotterbeck and Waldemar Anton. Konstantinos Karetsas and Julian Ryerson provide the width as wing-backs, while Felix Nmecha and Jobe Bellingham control the center of the park. Maximilian Beier and Daniel Svensson sit just behind Fábio Silva, giving Dortmund two players to link midfield and attack around a lone central striker.
Dortmund confirmed starting XI (3-4-2-1): Gregor Kobel, Julian Ryerson, Daniel Svensson, Nico Schlotterbeck, Waldemar Anton, Joane Gadou, Felix Nmecha, Joey Veerman, Fábio Silva, Jobe Bellingham, Maximilian Beier. Coach: Niko Kovač.

items.title: Why is Jude Bellingham not starting for Real Madrid vs PSV in the 2026-27 Champions League?
items.description:
Jude Bellingham begins Real Madrid's Champions League match against PSV on the bench, in a decision that reportedly responds to his heavy workload this season. 
Jude Bellingham is not part of Real Madrid’s starting lineup for the Champions League clash against PSV Eindhoven at the Santiago Bernabeu, a surprise on matchday five of the league phase. The England midfielder begins the match on the bench, in a decision that appears to come from Jose Mourinho himself.



The move seems to be purely sporting. Mourinho is reportedly giving Bellingham a rest to manage his workload, and the player is neither injured nor suspended. That explanation fits with the numbers, as Bellingham arrives at the PSV match after a heavy workload. 



This season he has appeared in 17 matches for Real Madrid between LaLiga and the Champions League, starting 16 of them, with an average of roughly 82 minutes per game.



In his place, Arda Guler enters the midfield, in a slightly more withdrawn role than Bellingham’s, behind an attack of Vinicius Junior, Yan Diomande and Kylian Mbappe.




📋✅ ¡Nuestro XI inicial!🆚 @PSV pic.twitter.com/XGjFbydvd4— Real Madrid C.F. (@realmadrid) November 24, 2026




Real Madrid arrive with a perfect record in the league phase, having won all four matches for 12 points, which leaves them second behind Paris Saint-Germain only on goal difference. PSV, meanwhile, sit 25th with four points and need a positive result to improve their chances of reaching the knockout stages.



Bellingham reportedly close to renewing with Real Madrid


        


The decision to rest Bellingham comes at a time when his future at the club appears to be close to settled. According to reports from Fabrizio Romano, Real Madrid and the England midfielder have reached a verbal agreement on a new five-year contract that would keep him at the Bernabeu until 2031, with the formalities still being finalized.



His current deal runs until the summer of 2029, so the extension would add two more years to his stay. The deal has not been officially announced by the club, although reports suggest that the announcement could come not long from now.



For now, Bellingham will watch the start of the match against PSV from the bench, but his place in Mourinho’s plans seems far from being in doubt. The rest should help him stay fresh for the busy stretch ahead, while also making him a strong option to reinforce the team whenever Mourinho feels it is necessary.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s mother Dolores Aveiro reveals major update on possible Portugal return after international retirement
items.description:
Ronaldo's mother's latest reported comments offer a clearer indication of where the 41-year-old stands following a difficult end to his 23-year career with the national team. 
Cristiano Ronaldo’s international future has taken another significant turn after his mother, Dolores Aveiro, addressed the possibility of him reversing his decision to retire from Portugal. Her latest reported comments offer a clearer indication of where the veteran stands following a difficult end to his 23-year career with the national team.



The five-time Ballon d’Or winner announced his retirement on November 5, 2026, bringing an end to one of the most successful international careers in soccer history. However, the circumstances surrounding his departure, particularly his disagreement with head coach Jorge Jesus, have continued to generate debate in Portugal.



Ronaldo finished his international career with 234 appearances and 146 goals, both men’s world records. He also collected 141 victories with Portugal and helped the national team win three major trophies: Euro 2016 and the UEFA Nations League in 2019 and 2025.



His journey began in August 2003, when he made his senior debut against Kazakhstan. Although his first major tournament ended in disappointment with the defeat to Greece in the Euro 2004 final, he eventually became the central figure in the country’s transformation into an international trophy winner.



Cristiano Ronaldo celebrates his goal for Portugal



Ronaldo’s final major tournament was the 2026 World Cup, where he scored three goals in five appearances. His final international strike came against Croatia in the Round of 32 on July 2, while his last appearance for the Selecao was a 1-0 Nations League victory over Wales on September 24.



Disagreement with Jorge Jesus contributed to his departure



Ronaldo’s retirement followed a breakdown in relations with Portugal head coach Jorge Jesus. The disagreement reportedly began after the forward was left on the bench against Norway in September, despite believing he had an understanding with the manager that he would receive around 30 minutes of playing time.



After warming up without being introduced, Ronaldo reportedly became frustrated with the situation. He subsequently left Portugal’s training camp in Copenhagen after being informed that he would not start the following fixture against Denmark.



Pedro Proenca, Cristiano Ronaldo, and Jorge Jesus



Although Jesus was reportedly preparing to include the veteran forward in his November plans, Ronaldo announced his retirement before the squad was revealed. In his farewell message, he insisted: “I leave with my head held high, proud of the path I have taken and knowing that I gave everything I had for Portugal.”



Dolores Aveiro reveals Ronaldo’s intention



Dolores Aveiro’s latest comments suggest that the possibility of Ronaldo returning to international soccer is effectively off the table. “Cristiano Ronaldo has made his final decision and isn’t considering reversing his international retirement.”, she said in an interview with 365Scores Arabic.



The reported remarks reinforce the impression that the former Portugal captain has no plans to reconsider his choice, despite the possibility of a future reconciliation with the national team. His attention remains on club soccer with Al-Nassr, where he is continuing his pursuit of 1,000 career goals.



Dolores Aveiro (mãe de CR7): "Claro que o Cristiano Ronaldo ficou triste, enganaram-no e eu também estou triste. Foi uma derrota [contra a Dinamarca] e foi bem feita, fiquei contente."Está aí o vosso capitão. E ainda manda a mãe. Nem é homenzinho para dizer publicamente o que… pic.twitter.com/xo1ifXZH64— O Fura-Redes (@OFuraRedes) November 16, 2026 



Aveiro had already attracted considerable attention with her comments about the circumstances surrounding her son’s departure. Speaking at an event at Sporting CP’s Estadio Jose Alvalade on November 16, she claimed Ronaldo had been “deceived” and disrespected by the national team, adding that she was pleased Portugal had subsequently suffered a 4-1 defeat to Denmark.

items.title: Copa America returns to USA in 2028: Why the USMNT isn’t qualified yet and how it can earn a spot
items.description:
The Copa America returns to the United States in 2028, but the USMNT must earn its place through the 2027 Gold Cup, with no automatic spot confirmed yet. 
The Copa America is heading back to the United States in 2028, but the host nation will have to earn its place in the field. CONMEBOL and Concacaf announced an extension of their strategic partnership to organize the 49th edition together, scheduled from June 9 to July 9, 2028, after the two confederations teamed up for the 2024 tournament.



The competition will feature 16 national teams, made up of the 10 CONMEBOL members and six Concacaf representatives. Unlike the last edition, which the U.S. also hosted, Concacaf has stated that its six teams will qualify based on sporting merit, which means the USMNT has no automatic berth confirmed and will need to earn its way in like everyone else.



The path runs through the 2027 Concacaf Gold Cup, played between June 17 and July 11, 2027. The USMNT has already secured its place in that tournament through the Nations League, where it won its quarterfinal series.



The Gold Cup will use a new format, with 16 teams split into two groups of eight, each team playing four group matches and the top four from each group advancing to a single-match knockout phase, starting with the quarterfinals. The draw is set for April 8, 2027.




Concacaf President Victor Montagliani announces the extension of our strategic partnership with CONMEBOL to co-organize the 2028 Copa América in the United States.Six Concacaf national teams will earn their place through the 2027 Concacaf Gold Cup.🏆▶️ Watch his message pic.twitter.com/rgDj9LjjW1— Concacaf (@Concacaf) November 24, 2026




What remains unclear is exactly how Gold Cup results will translate into the six Copa America berths. Concacaf said that the qualification mechanisms for its national teams, along with the host cities, venues and match schedule, will be announced in the near future.



For the USMNT, that means a deep run in the Gold Cup is the only confirmed route to a Copa America at home, and one that will test the squad less than a year after the 2026 World Cup.


        


USA chases a sixth Copa America appearance



The United States has taken part in the Copa America five times: in 1993, 1995, 2007, 2016 and 2024. Its best finish is fourth place, reached in 1995 and again in 2016, when it hosted the Centenario edition and lost in the semifinals to Argentina before falling to Colombia in the third-place match.



The U.S. was also host in 2024, but failed to advance beyond the group stage on home soil, a result that will add pressure to its 2028 campaign if it secures qualification.



It remains the only country outside CONMEBOL to have hosted the tournament, which is why the USMNT will want to be on the field when it returns in 2028 for a sixth appearance.

items.title: Lionel Messi gets different treatment from MLS referees, former Inter Miami boss Phil Neville claims
items.description:
Phil Neville, who coached Inter Miami before Lionel Messi arrived, says the referee's decision on the ball incident against Columbus Crew might have been different if another player had been involved. 
Phil Neville has added his voice to the debate around Lionel Messi and the officiating in Inter Miami’s 3-0 defeat to Columbus Crew in Game 1 of the MLS Cup Playoffs. 



The former Inter Miami coach reportedly suggested that the Argentine is judged differently from other players, particularly after the decision not to send him off for an incident just before halftime.



The play came late in the first half, with Miami already down to ten men and trailing 1-0. Columbus forward Gonzalo Tapia had stepped in front of Messi to stop him from taking a quick throw-in, and Messi responded by throwing the ball at his face.



Referee Allen Chapman showed yellow cards to both players, explaining that the force was negligible and did not amount to violent conduct. Against that backdrop, Jose Armando Rodriguez of Deporte Total USA reported that, for Neville, the referee’s decision was not the right one because it involved Messi. “If it’s Ian Smith throwing the ball, he gets sent off. Lionel Messi doesn’t get sent off,” said the Portland coach, referring to one of his own defenders.



Lionel Messi y Gonzalo Tapia recibieron tarjeta amarilla después de esta acción en la banda.(vía @MLS por Apple TV) pic.twitter.com/kvMAjakAUv— ESPN Deportes (@ESPNDeportes) November 22, 2026 



He also reportedly said that referees have approached certain situations differently since Messi’s arrival to the USA. “Since Messi arrived in MLS, there are situations that referees have handled with common sense,” added the current Portland Timbers coach.



Neville’s words carry extra weight because of his history with the club. He was Inter Miami’s last coach before Messi joined, having been dismissed in June 2023, just before the arrival of the player who would transform the franchise.


        


Inter Miami face a complicated outlook heading into Game 2



The picture is difficult for the defending champions, who now trail 1-0 in a best-of-three series after the heavy loss at Nu Stadium. Game 2 is scheduled for Friday, November 27, at 8 p.m. ET in Columbus, where Inter Miami must avoid defeat to stay alive. A loss would end their title defense in the First Round, while Columbus only need one more win to advance.



If Miami manage to win in Columbus, the series would be level and head to a decisive Game 3 back at Nu Stadium on December 2. In Round One there is no extra time, so if Game 2 is level after 90 minutes, the winner will be decided by a penalty shootout.



The winner of the series would then move on to the Conference Semifinals, set for December 5-6, against the winner of the New England Revolution vs Philadelphia Union series.

items.title: Timothy Weah: ‘I don’t want to beg to be back in the national team’
items.description: Winger has not played for the USMNT since the World Cup and believes good club form is his route back into the squadThis was the USMNT’s summer. By extension, it was also that of the 26 players selected by Mauricio Pochettino to represent the nation at a home World Cup. It didn’t live up to expectations for all of them, and certainly not for Timothy Weah. “Obviously this summer wasn’t the best for me,” he says.Weah was one of eight players in the squad to have started all four of the US’s matches in Qatar in 2022. He remained a regular heading into this tournament but would ultimately start only one game in a campaign that came to an end at the hands of Belgium in the last 16. “In every career you have moments where you’re a bit down, and you’re a bit in your head about things. I think the World Cup was definitely that for me,” Weah says. “On a personal level, I had to take a back seat and figure out where my place was in the squad.” Continue reading...

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo and Al-Nassr’s key obstacle to defend Saudi Pro League title traced back to one major source in explosive verdict
items.description:
Despite remaining among the leading sides in the Saudi Pro League, frustration is building around the decisions shaping the club’s direction, with supporters increasingly questioning who should be held accountable. 
Cristiano Ronaldo’s future at Al-Nassr has come under renewed scrutiny as the Saudi club faces growing financial pressure and questions over its ability to compete for major honors. Despite remaining among the leading sides in the Saudi Pro League, frustration is building around the decisions shaping the club’s direction, with supporters increasingly questioning who should be held accountable.



The debate has intensified following Al-Nassr’s recent defeat to Al-Ahli, which exposed concerns about squad depth, recruitment and the club’s wider ambitions. While Ronaldo’s enormous wages and performances have also attracted criticism, one particular argument has shifted attention towards the people making the biggest decisions behind the scenes.



Al-Nassr has reportedly accumulated liabilities exceeding 800 million Saudi Riyals, equivalent to around $212-$213 million, following years of expensive recruitment and substantial player contracts. The financial pressure has prompted tighter oversight and restrictions on transfer activity, leaving manager Ange Postecoglou with limited opportunities to strengthen his squad.



The situation has become particularly frustrating given the club’s ambitions after winning the Saudi Pro League title in 2025-26. The team currently sits third with 28 points from 12 matches, two points behind leaders Al-Hilal, although its rivals have a game in hand.



PositionClubMatchesW-D-LGoal DifferencePoints1.Al-Hilal1110-0-1+23302.Al-Qadsiah129-1-2+20283.Al-Nassr129-1-2+15284.Al-Ahli128-0-4+11245.Al-Ittihad117-3-1+1024Current Saudi Pro League standings



The club has still enjoyed an impressive campaign offensively, with Ronaldo scoring eight league goals and Joao Felix contributing seven assists. However, defensive vulnerabilities and a lack of midfield balance have become concerns, particularly following the departure of Marcelo Brozovic.



Recent defeat increases pressure on Ronaldo and Postecoglou



Al-Nassr’s 3-1 defeat to Al-Ahli on November 20 brought those weaknesses into sharper focus. Ronaldo opened the scoring but subsequently missed a penalty, allowing Al-Ahli to recover and eventually secure all three points.



Former Al-Nassr player Fuad Anwar criticized the Portuguese forward’s contribution, arguing that his missed spot-kick helped shift the momentum. “But he (Ronaldo) failed to convert the penalty that would have allowed Al-Nassr to stay in control, and that is what gave the Al-Ahli players the motivation to get back into the match, equalize and then win,” he told Arriyadiyah.









Anwar also defended Postecoglou, pointing to the club’s inability to strengthen during the summer transfer window. He believes the Australian coach has been left working with insufficient squad depth, particularly after Brozovic departed.



New source becomes main target of criticism



The wider frustration has now turned towards Al-Nassr’s ownership, with Saudi sports analyst Sultan Al-Otaibi delivering a particularly blunt assessment of the situation. In a post shared on social media, he argued that responsibility ultimately rests with those controlling the club’s major decisions.



“The primary and ultimate blame for Al Nassr’s problems lies solely with their owners. They’re the ones who appoint the officials, they’re the ones who approve the deals and contracts, and they’re the ones who reject them,” Al-Otaibi wrote on X (formerly Twitter).



Cristiano Ronaldo of Al Nassr celebrates with the Saudi Pro League Trophy.



His comments reflect growing criticism of the Public Investment Fund (PIF), which holds full ownership of Al-Nassr. Critics argue that the financial restrictions imposed by the fund have prevented the club from addressing important weaknesses, despite its continued ambitions to challenge for domestic and continental honors.



PIF’s involvement in financial supervision has also raised questions about the club’s executive structure. Reports of internal changes and restrictions on the authority of senior officials have added to concerns about stability and long-term planning.
